paragraphs: Friend, here's what Paul wants Rome to know: the gospel is not a new idea and it is not a small one. God promised it beforehand through His prophets in the Holy Scriptures (Romans 1:2), and it is all about His Son, Jesus Christ our Lord, who was declared with power to be the Son of God by His resurrection from the dead (Romans 1:4). So when you open your Bible, you are not holding some last-minute plan. You are holding a promise God made a long time ago and kept.

And look at how Paul lives that out. He is grateful before he asks for anything, he prays for the believers constantly, and he longs to be mutually encouraged by their faith (Romans 1:8-12). This man is an apostle, and he still says he needs them. I think that's the kind of baker God is making: thankful, praying, and glad to be strengthened by the people next to you. Nobody in the Dorinverse bakes alone, and I would know, because I tried it in a junk drawer.

Then Paul says it plain: 'I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes…' (Romans 1:16). EVERYONE who believes. Not the best, not the smartest, not the ones with their act together. The gospel reveals the righteousness of God that comes by faith from start to finish, just as it is written: 'The righteous will live by faith.' (Romans 1:17). So the big idea is this: you don't earn your place at God's table, you trust the One who already made room for you.
